Allowing facilities to be sited more closely than 50 miles apart concentrates risks of traffic, health, and safety impacts to the surrounding communities. Figure 5-2 illustrates the siting decisions made by the BILT model. The first set of results in Figure 5-2 shows the sites of facilities without allowing the model to stack. The green lines indicate the assignment of feedstock to facilities. In cases where two facilities are used in the pathways (e.g., soybeans to soybean oil and soybean oil to RD), the movement of the intermediate product is shown with white lines. Purple circles indicate the first facility in the pathway, and orange circles the second. 36 Figure 5-2 Production Facility Siting Decisions from BILT Model for Renewable Diesel (RD) and Biodiesel (BD) Cases Facilities within this analysis that process waste resources have a capacity of processing 100 MT per day. While swine manure resources are concentrated in the center of the nation, sludge resources are available nationwide. However, most counties do not have sufficient resources available to support a 100 MT/day facility. At the other end of the supply scale, a few counties 37 (primarily urban) produce much more sludge than a single facility can handle. The map on the left in Figure 5-3 shows the counties that could support 100 MT/day, and the map on the right illustrates the size of facilities that could be supported by the available biomass. For BILT modeling runs, “stacking” is where multiple facilities of a given size are at the same location with an economy of scale factor used. The results of these runs allowing multiple facility sizes and stacking of up to 5 are shown in Figure 5-4.
